- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in the following 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the first 3–5 days of a new trend; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for the first 3–5 days of upward moves.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; use a 1–2% upward bias for the next 3–7 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Model often fails to account for sentiment reversal near the end of the forecast horizon; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the last 3–5 days if sentiment turns bearish.
